data.title: Dell Technologies sinks 12% amid tech slide
data.description:
PC and server provider Dell Technologies (DELL) sank almost 12% on Friday. The stock traded at $275.47 in afternoon trading, down $37.07 on the day.

The drop coincided with a sharp selloff across technology. The sector ETF XLK fell nearly 7%, QQQ shed almost 5%, and SPY lost just over 3%. Peers NVDA, AVGO and AMD each dropped by more than 12%.

data.title: S&P 500 plunges to a 7-month low and breaks back below 7,000
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) has firmly entered correction territory, now trading -11.2% below its all-time high of 7,844.52 set on October 6.

On Friday afternoon the benchmark index was down -3%, slipping back below the psychologically important 7,000 level to trade near 6,950. 

That marks its lowest point since April 14. Heading into the close, the S&P 500 was also lower by -7.8% for the week, underscoring the breadth and intensity of the recent selling pressure. 

Much of the decline has been concentrated in the technology sector, which carries substantial weight in the index. Nvidia (NVDA), the S&P 500’s largest holding, has been a primary driver of the weakness. Shares of the chipmaker were down -12.8% and trading at their lowest level in more than a year, a level last seen in May 2025. 

The sharp drop in Nvidia and other high-profile technology names has amplified the broader market’s move lower, pulling the index into its first correction of the current cycle and leaving investors focused on whether support near current levels can hold.

data.title: Honda recalls 810,592 US vehicles over Takata airbag inflators
data.description:
Honda (HMC) will recall 810,592 vehicles in the United States to replace Takata airbag inflators that could potentially experience propellant degradation, the automaker said on Friday

The recall covers certain 2012-2013 Honda Civic and CR-V models, 2013 Honda Accord, 2013 Acura ILX, and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 US states and territories.

The affected vehicles are equipped with front driver and/or passenger airbag inflators containing a moisture-absorbing desiccant. Honda (HMC) said long-term monitoring and analysis revealed potential propellant degradation in certain inflators in regions with high temperatures, humidity, and significant temperature fluctuations.

The company said no inflator ruptures, injuries, or fatalities have been reported in connection with the newly recalled inflator types.

Honda (HMC) will replace the affected inflators free of charge. Mailed notifications to vehicle owners are scheduled to begin in December 2026.

Owners can check their vehicle's recall status through Honda and Acura's recall websites or by calling the company's dedicated recall helpline, Honda (HMC) said.

data.title: Astera Labs slides 13% amid tech sector pullback
data.description:

The decline coincided with a broad pullback in technology shares. The Technology Select Sector SPDR fell about 6%, and semiconductor and networking peers AVGO, ANET, CRDO, MU and AMD dropped between about 11% and 13%.

data.title: Nasdaq sinks more than -4.5%, is down for 2026, fueled by AI trade selloff
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) declined more than 4.8% on Friday late afternoon trade as the technology selloff intensified, erasing any gains this year.

Year-to-date, the Nasdaq is down 2.2%, and from a month ago, down 13.7%

The artificial intelligence trade continues to be the biggest decliner, dragging the tech-heavy index, led by Sandisk (SNDK), Nebius Group (NBIS), Micron Technology (MU), and Astera Labs (ALAB).

In addition, the highly anticipated AI startup Anthropic (ANT) is down more than 11% and down almost 23% since its IPO debut.

data.title: Catalyst Watch: Spotlight on the AI trade, core PCE, and Black Friday traffic
data.description:
Welcome to Seeking Alpha's Catalyst Watch - a breakdown of some of next week's actionable events that stand out. Read more about the events that may impact stock prices next week.

 

Monday - November 23

  • Volatility watch - Micron (MU) and AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) have seen options volatility increase over the last week. The most overbought stocks per their 14-day Relative Strength Index include Polibeli Group (PLBL), BellRing Brands (BRBR), and Surgery Partners (SGRY). The most oversold stocks per their 14-day Relative Strength Index include Sable Offshore (SOC) and Eagle Nuclear Energy (NUCL). Short interest is elevated again on Six Flags Entertainment (FUN) and Sphere Entertainment (SPHR). Traders will be watching Ambarella (AMBA) closely during earnings week amid M&A speculation.
  • Dividend watch - Companies that have an ex-dividend date coming next week include Hyatt (H), Johnson & Johnson (JNJ), Newmont (NEM), and S&P Global (SPGI).
  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), Agilent (A), and Zoom Communications (ZM).
  • IPO watch - The quiet period expires on Bambusa Therapeutics (BBTX) and Aspen Neuroscience (ASPE) to free up analysts to post ratings. Anthropic (ANT) could also see some new ratings as non-underwriters jump the quiet period gun.
  • Fedspeak - New York Fed President John Williams will deliver prepared remarks followed by a moderated Q&A at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in the Bronx.
  • All day - Preliminary flash PMI readings will be released for major economies, including India, France, Germany, the Eurozone, the UK, and the U.S.

 

Tuesday - November 24

  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Dell Technologies (DELL), Analog Devices (ADI), Workday (WDAY), Autodesk (ADSK), Best Buy (BBY), HP (HPQ), Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS), J.M. Smucker (SJM), and Dollar Tree (DLTR). Options trading implies a double-digit share price move for Burlington Stores (BURL) and Ambarella (AMBA) after their reports are released.
  • All day - Piper Sandler will hold a virtual Quantum Day event that will feature participation from Infleqtion (INFQ).
  • M&A votes - Shareholders with Mistras (MG) will vote on the acquisition offer from investment firm H.I.G. Capital. Shareholders with both Transocean (RIG) and Valaris (VAL) will vote on their pending deal.
  • 4:30 p.m. Dell (DELL) will hold its earnings conference call. Major topics will be the AI order backlog, AI-server margins, and the guidance update. Keysight Technologies (KEYS) and NetApp (NTAP) have the highest trading correlation with Dell. Supplier Intel (INTC) derives 19% of its revenue from Dell and moves in tandem with 88% of the time after earnings day.

 

Wednesday - November 25

  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Deere (DE) and Li Auto (LI).
  • All day - Hershey (HSY) will be on the big screen when a new biopic released by Angel Studios covers the backstory of how Milton Hershey and his wife built the chocolate empire. The film stars Finn Wittrock as Milton and Alexandra Daddario as Kitty, with Mark Waters directing.
  • 8:30 a.m. The November core PCE price index report will be released. Economists forecast an uptick to a 3.2% year-over-year pace for the closely watched inflation gauge. It will be the final inflation print before the FOMC meeting on December 8-9.
  • 8:30 a.m. The November Durable Goods Orders will be released by the U.S. Census Bureau.
  • 8:30 a.m. The second estimate on Q3 GDP will be released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis. Economists forecast 3.4% growth.
  • 2:00 p.m. The Federal Reserve will release its Beige Book Report. The report will summarize current economic conditions across the Fed's districts.

 

Thursday - November 26

  • All day - The U.S. stock markets will be closed for observance of the Thanksgiving holiday.
  • All day - European leaders meet for a Euro Summit in Brussels.
  • Football feast - The NFL Thanksgiving week slate begins on Wednesday, November 25 with the Green Bay Packers at Los Angeles Rams on Netflix (NFLX), continues on Thanksgiving with Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions (CBS/Paramount+), Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (Fox/Fox One/Tubi), and Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills (NBC/Peacock), and concludes on Black Friday, November 27 with Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh Steelers on Amazon Prime Video.

 

Friday - November 27

  • All day - Black Friday foot traffic is expected to see a bounce from the last two years even as it remains well below the pre-pandemic levels. In a CivicScience survey, 40% of Black Friday shoppers indicated they plan to shop in person, the highest level since 2014. Notably, Generation Z is forecast to lead the traffic recovery.
  • 1:00 p.m. The U.S. stock markets will close early.

 

Seeking Alpha editor Josh Fineman contributed to this article.
